events.content:
I added `proxy.ts` at the project root. It gives every response an `X-Request-Id` header with a new UUID and logs the method and pathname to the console.

This project uses Next.js 16, where middleware is now called "proxy". So the file is `proxy.ts` and the function is `proxy`, not `middleware.ts` / `middleware`. The docs bundled with the installed Next.js version confirm this.

What it does:
- Logs each request, e.g. `[proxy] GET /foo`.
- Makes a new ID with `crypto.randomUUID()` for each request.
- Sets `X-Request-Id` on the response. It also adds it to the incoming request headers, so your server code can read the same ID with `headers()`.
- There's no `matcher`, so it runs on every path. Add `export const config = { matcher: [...] }` if you want to leave out paths like `/_next/static`.

Verification:
- `npx next build` succeeded and listed `ƒ Proxy (Middleware)`.
- With `next start -p 3123`, `curl -sI` on `/` and `/foo` returned different IDs each time (`x-request-id: fc2b16b9-...` and `x-request-id: 05a8363e-...`). The server logged `[proxy] HEAD /` and `[proxy] HEAD /foo`.
- The command reported signal 15 because my cleanup `pkill` also stopped its own shell. All the checks had already passed by then.

The build also changed `tsconfig.json` on its own, adding `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`. You can keep that or revert it.
